transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-13
Time: 08:30 PT / 15:30 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Rajesh Patel (Redwood SE), Chris Nguyen (Redwood CSM), Marta Lopez (Sundial Head of Data), Tom Reeves (Sundial Platform), Ibrahim Malik (Sundial PM), Emily Zhao (Sundial SRE)

Summary (auto): brief stability/regression review, confirm fallback and rollout playbook, next steps for benchmarks and prompt prioritization.

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: okay, hi everyone, thanks for joining today, um, agenda is the stability gate that tripped last week, quick root cause hypotheses, and then a fallback playbook so your service doesn't see errors in production.
[00:17] Marta Lopez: yep, thanks Lena. we saw a jump in inference errors around May 7th during the morning peak, about, uh, 8 to 12,000 requests per hour, error rate from 0.2% to 2.6%.
[00:29] Tom Reeves: and just to be clear the traffic pattern was bursty, not steady - a lot of small spikes from the mobile app.
[00:40] Rajesh Patel: thanks. we pulled the traces - initial look points to two correlated things: model OOMs on the dedicated node pool when sequence length spiked, and a mis-specified KV cache retention that caused repeated cold starts.
[00:58] Emily Zhao: when you say "KV cache" you mean the key-value recursion cache? sometimes our logs label it K V cash, haha, but yes we saw cache churn.
[01:12] Rajesh Patel: right, K V cache churn. also some requests fell through to the large-llm variant which pushes memory. we think a combination of quantization path and kernel selection thrash under that burst pattern.
[01:28] Ibrahim Malik: quick question — this was on your hosted environment or on the Dedicated test pool? we pinned version v1.4.2 for the poc.
[01:36] Lena Ortiz: this was on Dedicated pool in your test workspace. we had a canary of hosted fallback but it didn't trigger because routing policy didn't detect the transient spike fast enough.
[01:50] Marta Lopez: so what you're saying is the fallback exists but the routing policy threshold is too conservative for bursty traffic.
[01:57] Rajesh Patel: exactly. and we also saw a couple of guardrail false positives — some rejects that should've passed, likely due to prompt tokenization edge cases.
[02:12] Tom Reeves: can you give an example?
[02:16] Rajesh Patel: sure — one was a prompt with nested JSON and lots of escape chars. tokenization changed the sequence length estimate so the runtime routed the request to the longer-context path unexpectedly.
[02:30] Marta Lopez: ugh, that one's in our top 50 prompt templates. we'll pull that set.
[02:36] Chris Nguyen: great, captured. next up, fallback playbook. we proposed an immediate two-tier approach: 1) aggressive routing to a smaller quantized model for short transient spikes, 2) automating a fast circuit-breaker at the ingress to avoid thrashing.
[02:54] Lena Ortiz: Rajesh, can you talk through the canary test we suggested?
[02:58] Rajesh Patel: yeah — the plan is spin up a small, lower-memory model (gpt-small-quant) in a parallel capacity pool, route 2% of traffic during peak for 24 hours and compare latencies/errors. if error delta is below threshold, increase to 10% and then flip route when stable.
[03:18] Emily Zhao: what about quality degradation? product won't accept a lot of hallucinations.
[03:23] Rajesh Patel: agreed, we run a quick scoring pass on a holdout set (you said 5k historical prompts) and ensure answer similarity above 0.92 F1-ish metric — we can tune thresholds but we won't auto-fallback if quality drops below your tolerance.
[03:40] Ibrahim Malik: can we also do a per-route scoring so we can see exact examples where fallback changed the output?
[03:46] Lena Ortiz: yes, Redwood console exposes per-request diffs and delta scoring in the trial; we'll enable that on the canary.
[03:54] Marta Lopez: okay. quick qualification — time to decision? we need to know whether we will accept Dedicated as long-term. SREs want to see consistent under 100ms p95 for short prompts.
[04:08] Tom Reeves: and cost matters — if fallback adds 20% unit cost we're going to need to see economic tradeoffs.
[04:15] Lena Ortiz: understoood. we'll produce a cost-latency tradeoff table. Rajesh, you'll run the 3-model benchmark (large, medium-quant, small-quant) with the bursty pattern and 8k token windows.
[04:29] Rajesh Patel: yes — I'll run it and include per-token cost estimate plus GPU retention numbers.
[04:36] [04:36] Marta Lopez: the guardrail false positives — is that rule-based or model-based guardrail? we have both.
[04:42] Rajesh Patel: mostly rule-based thresholding plus a safety classifier. classifier had a higher false-positive on templates with code blocks and base64-like strings. tokenizer tricked it.
[04:52] Ibrahim Malik: so what's short-term mitigation to reduce FP while we retrain/re-tune?
[04:57] Rajesh Patel: two levers: loosen threshold for those templates, and add a sanitizer step to normalize escapes before scoring. both are quick config changes.
[05:08] Emily Zhao: will sanitizer affect latency?
[05:11] Rajesh Patel: negligible — a few ms per request, but we'll measure.
[05:15] Tom Reeves: logs — we'll need full traces with kernel selection flags, and the dump of the K V cache churn metric. can you share where to drop logs?
[05:24] Chris Nguyen: yes, drop to the secure bucket link we sent in the onboarding doc; Lena will re-send the link after the call.
[05:32] Lena Ortiz: sending link after; we also will attach the raw canary results when ready.
[05:36] Marta Lopez: for the canary timeline, can we do the 2% traffic run Friday May 21st during your off-peak?
[05:44] Rajesh Patel: Friday works, but we should align on peak window and the traffic generator config. I'll share the benchmark harness config.
[05:51] Ibrahim Malik: question about rollback — if the canary shows regression in quality but not errors, do we keep it?
[05:58] Rajesh Patel: no, the playbook says we require both error reduction and quality parity above threshold. if quality regresses, we'll keep routing to primary and then run a tuned small-quant candidate.
[06:11] Marta Lopez: one more ops ask — can you provide a pre-baked circuit-breaker snippet for our ingress to call the Redwood control API? our infra folks prefer to keep routing rules close to the edge.
[06:23] Lena Ortiz: yes we'll provide a minimal webhook snippet and a design doc.
[06:28] Tom Reeves: perfect. also, can you give us the delta pricing for Dedicated reserved vs Hosted on demand at the projected throughput of 1.2M tokens/day?
[06:38] Lena Ortiz: I'll include that in the cost-latency table.
[06:41] Marta Lopez: regarding prompt prioritization — we'll mark the top 50 templates and highlight 12 that cause highest user-facing errors.
[06:49] Chris Nguyen: noted. we'll also tag them in the console so Rajesh's benchmark can include those templates.
[06:56] Rajesh Patel: quick note — kernel selection thrash is somewhat hardware-specific. for Dedicated we recommend pinning to a quantization-friendly kernel on the pool to avoid thrash; I'll add recommended startup flags.
[07:09] Emily Zhao: does that require a redeploy of the runtime?
[07:12] Rajesh Patel: minimal restart of the pool nodes, not full redeploy; it's in our ops playbook.
[07:18] Ibrahim Malik: are there any compliance flags — we have to show audit logs for prompt routing changes during the pilot.
[07:24] Lena Ortiz: Redwood console keeps an audit trail for routing rules and model swaps — we'll set retention to 90 days for the pilot.
[07:33] Marta Lopez: excellent. any blockers we haven't covered?
[07:37] Tom Reeves: we need the infra traces and the secure bucket link.
[07:40] Lena Ortiz: will send both today.
[07:43] Chris Nguyen: action recaps — Rajesh runs benchmarks and provides harness; Marta compiles prompt set; Tom dumps traces; Lena sends pricing and links; follow-up call next Friday post-canary.
[07:58] Ibrahim Malik: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:02] Lena Ortiz: thanks all, we'll send notes and the playbook. bye.

Meeting end.
